one_liner: Google's C++ PDF engine behind Chromium's viewer; about 2.5x faster text extraction than Poppler's pdftotext.
what_it_does: PDFium is Chromium's PDF library: it parses, renders (AGG rasterizer by default, an experimental Skia backend), extracts text with per-character boxes, fills forms (optional XFA and JavaScript through V8) and edits and saves PDFs. The public interface is a C API (fpdfview.h, fpdf_text.h, fpdf_edit.h and others) over C++20 internals: FPDF_InitLibrary, FPDF_LoadMemDocument, FPDF_LoadPage, FPDFText_LoadPage, then FPDFText_GetText or FPDFText_GetBoundedText. It is not a drop-in for pdftotext: no text CLI ships (pdfium_test only rasterises pages), so you write the per-page extraction loop yourself or use a binding such as pypdfium2, the one the benchmark used.
how_it_is_fast: Text extraction (CPDF_TextPage) is a single pass over the page's text objects in content-stream order: each object is compared with the previous one and spaces or line breaks are generated from geometry thresholds (ProcessInsertObject), with no word, line or block clustering and no reading-order sort. Poppler's default pdftotext mode (TextOutputDev::coalesce) builds words, lines, blocks and flows and topologically sorts blocks into reading order, so part of the measured gap is less layout work rather than a faster parser. The benchmarked binary is a Clang release build from bblanchon/pdfium-binaries (is_debug=false, Chromium toolchain, PartitionAlloc off, no V8/XFA) running in-process, while Poppler runs as a separate process; no SIMD-specific text code was found. Upstream checks changes for speed regressions with SafetyNet (testing/tools/safetynet_compare.py), which compares two PDFium versions by time or instruction counts on a set of PDFs, Linux only.
when_to_use: Bulk text extraction from born-digital PDFs (LaTeX papers, generated reports) whose content-stream order is already reading order: 1.59 s against 4.01 s for pdftotext over 14 documents, with the suite's top quality score (95%).
Products that must embed a PDF engine under a permissive licence: BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE also carries the Apache-2.0 text), where Poppler is GPL and MuPDF is AGPL-3.0 or commercial.
Applications needing rendering, text with character boxes (FPDFText_GetCharBox), forms and page editing from one library, from C/C++, Python (pypdfium2), .NET (NuGet) or WASM.
Cross-platform shipping without building it yourself: pdfium-binaries publishes weekly prebuilt libraries for Linux glibc and musl, macOS, Windows (x86, x64, arm64), Android, iOS and WASM.
when_not_to_use: Multi-column or complex layouts where reading order matters: PDFium emits content-stream order with no column analysis, while pdftotext's default mode reconstructs reading order and -layout preserves physical layout.
Parallel extraction inside one process: fpdfview.h states that none of the PDFium APIs are thread-safe, so every call must be serialised; use a process pool instead.
Teams that must build from source with their own toolchain: GN, Ninja and depot_tools with Chromium's Clang; GCC support is community patches only and MSVC patches are not accepted.

Opening untrusted PDFs in a privileged process: Chrome keeps shipping PDFium use-after-free fixes (CVE-2026-11303 to CVE-2026-11307, fixed in Chrome 149.0.7827.53, per search-result summaries); sandbox it the way Chrome does.
Tools that need raw PDF object access (dictionaries, streams, name trees): the public API does not expose it (crbug.com/pdfium/1694, per the pypdfium2 README).

integration.form: shared lib (static with pdf_is_complete_lib); usually consumed as prebuilt pdfium-binaries archives or pypdfium2 wheels
integration.dependencies: DEPS-pinned and vendored: FreeType, libjpeg-turbo, libpng, zlib, ICU, abseil, fast_float, simdutf, Highway, dragonbox, fp16, cpu_features, PartitionAlloc; OpenJPEG bundled unless use_system_libopenjpeg2; optional V8 (JavaScript and XFA) and Skia
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (default build), Clang under Chromium's toolchain policy, GN plus Ninja from depot_tools; GCC community patches only, no MSVC
integration.platforms: x64 default on Windows, Linux and macOS, x86 on Windows, arm for Android per README; pdfium-binaries adds Linux arm/arm64/x86/ppc64 and musl, Windows arm64, iOS and WASM; big-endian is not a priority
integration.thread_safety: None of the PDFium APIs are thread-safe (fpdfview.h): embedders must ensure only one PDFium call runs at a time; pypdfium2 repeats this as a known limitation.

gotchas: Harness noise (read this session): each cell is one time.time() run, and the four committed cache.json snapshots give pypdfium2 totals of 1.537 s, 3.970 s, 1.715 s and 1.591 s against pdftotext 4.039 s, 4.690 s, 4.539 s and 4.008 s; in the 2026-10-02 run (commit c323a47) 2201.00214 took 2.816 s instead of about 0.5 s, cutting the total advantage to 1.18x, while the per-document geometric mean stayed 2.3x to 2.5x in all four runs (derived from page data).

Not the same work: pypdfium2 runs in-process and returns content-stream-order text, while pdftotext is launched with subprocess after a temp-file write and does reading-order analysis; even charging the smallest pdftotext time (0.037 s) as fixed start-up cost on all 14 documents leaves about 3.49 s against 1.59 s (about 2.2x, derived from page data).

FPDFText_GetText, which pypdfium2's get_text_range calls, 'ignores characters without UCS-2 representations' and also returns characters outside the crop box; pypdfium2 points to get_text_bounded for full Unicode.

The quality comparison is asymmetric: pypdfium2 and pypdf output pass through the suite's own postprocess (ligature replacement, de-hyphenation, page-label removal) before scoring, while pdftotext and PyMuPDF are scored raw, so the 95% against 90% gap is partly the harness's cleanup (that Python work does count against PDFium's time).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against MuPDF, which ties it on text speed (1.604 s against 1.591 s) and is about 2x faster at image extraction, pick PDFium when the licence must be permissive rather than AGPL; against Poppler, pick PDFium for speed and licence unless you need reading-order reconstruction or a ready-made CLI. The path rasterizers in this category (Blend2D, ThorVG, Skia-class engines) do not parse PDF.
verified_claims_summary: In the independent py-pdf/benchmarks suite on an Intel Core i7-6700HQ, one timed run per document over 14 born-digital PDFs (7 to 134 pages), pypdfium2 5.13.0 with a prebuilt pdfium-binaries Clang release build extracted text in 1.591 s in total against 4.008 s for the distro Poppler 24.02.0 pdftotext binary run as a subprocess, about 2.5x (geometric mean 2.4x, derived from page data); only text extraction was measured, not rendering.
status_note: Actively developed as Chromium's PDF engine (the GitHub mirror chromium/pdfium, flagged archived since 2023-08-04, still lists commits to 2025-11-19; pdfium-binaries builds weekly and pypdfium2 5.14.0 shipped 2026-10-04); copyable under BSD-3-Clause, the numbers stand as tier B with harness caveats (one-shot timings, unequal text work) rather than flaws that invalidate them.
